data.title: Sunshine Oilsands Updates Investors on Alberta Court Judgment
data.description:
The latest update is out from Sunshine Oilsands ( (HK:2012) ).

Sunshine Oilsands Ltd. is an Alberta-incorporated company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The release does not specify its industry, primary products, services or market focus.

The Alberta Court of King’s Bench judgment, received on October 28, does not transfer legal ownership of the relevant assets but gives the Orphan Well Association powers to take over, manage and deal with them under court supervision. Sunshine Oilsands filed a notice of appeal on October 30; no hearing date is set, and the company says the appeal’s prospects face material uncertainty due to complex legal issues, arrears and the court’s discretionary powers.

data.title: Walnut Capital Proposes Eight-for-One Share Consolidation
data.description:
Walnut Capital Limited ( (HK:0905) ) has provided an announcement.

Walnut Capital Limited has proposed consolidating every eight issued and unissued shares of HK$0.01 each into one share of HK$0.08 each. The proposal requires shareholder approval at a special general meeting and remains conditional, so it may not proceed.

If effective, the board lot would change from 16,000 existing shares to 2,000 consolidated shares, in line with stated Main Board trading requirements. Based on the cited closing price, the theoretical consolidated-share price would be HK$2, while the estimated value of each revised board lot would be HK$4,000, versus HK$32,000 for a 16,000-share consolidated lot.

data.title: Yueyun Announces Agreements to Repurchase Stakes in Two Subsidiaries
data.description:
Guangdong Yueyun Transportation Co., Ltd. Class H ( (HK:3399) ) has issued an announcement.

On 19 November 2026, Guangzhou Company agreed to repurchase Shenzhen Communication’s 19% equity interest for RMB9,802,700 and cancel it through a capital reduction. Hong Kong Company conditionally agreed to repurchase Shenzhen Communication’s 3,420 shares, representing 19% of its issued shares, for HK$119,621,500 and cancel them; aggregate consideration is approximately RMB112,154,444 at the stated exchange rate.

Upon completion, the Company’s holding in each subsidiary would rise from 62% to approximately 76.54%, Jing Mei’s would rise from 19% to approximately 23.46%, and Shenzhen Communication would no longer hold equity in either company. The subsidiaries would remain non-wholly-owned and consolidated, while the aggregated repurchases are discloseable and connected transactions subject to reporting and announcement requirements but exempt from shareholder approval.

data.title: China Development Bank Financial Leasing Enters Agreement to Purchase About RMB2.271 Billion of IT Equipment
data.description:
China Development Bank Financial Leasing Co Ltd Class H ( (HK:1606) ) has provided an announcement.

China Development Bank Financial Leasing Co., Ltd. is a PRC-incorporated financial leasing company that conducts operating-lease business, including leasing information technology computer equipment to third-party lessees. The company acts as a lessor in the described arrangement.

On 19 November 2026, the company agreed to buy approximately 1,200 brand-new information technology computer equipment units from Guangdong Shuhuan for about RMB2.271 billion, intending to lease them to third-party lessees under operating-lease agreements after completion. When aggregated with previous transactions involving the same seller, the proposed purchase constitutes a major transaction subject to reporting, announcement, circular and shareholder approval requirements.

data.title: Guangdong Yueyun Signs RMB26,243,316 Photovoltaic EPC Contract
data.description:
Guangdong Yueyun Transportation Co., Ltd. Class H ( (HK:3399) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Guangdong Yueyun Transportation Company Limited is a transportation company with a New Energy Branch involved in expressway service-zone projects. On 19 November 2026, the branch signed a RMB26,243,316 tax-inclusive photovoltaic engineering, procurement and construction contract with Lulutong for the GF1 section of a distributed photovoltaic project at Guangdong Provincial GCGC Expressway service zones.

Phase I covers 21 pairs of service zones, with GF1 involving 11 pairs, and the contract includes photovoltaic design, equipment procurement, installation, testing, commissioning and connection to the company’s intelligent management system. Because Lulutong is indirectly controlled by the company’s controlling shareholder, GCGC, the agreement is a connected transaction subject to reporting and announcement requirements but exempt from shareholder approval and related circular requirements.

data.title: Great Eagle-Sino Land JV Wins Hong Kong Development Tender
data.description:
The latest update is out from Great Eagle Holdings ( (HK:0041) ).

Great Eagle Holdings and Sino Land established a joint venture with Great Eagle holding 25% and Sino Land 75%. On 19 November 2026, the Urban Renewal Authority awarded the tender to the JV’s wholly owned project company for upfront payments of HK$2,688 million.

The tender covers a composite development comprising residential units, residential parking spaces, a commercial portion and government accommodation. The release states that Great Eagle contributed HK$12.5 million to the initial deposit and HK$659.5 million to the second upfront payment, with those contributions treated as shareholder loans to the JV.

data.title: Lvji Technology Shareholders Approve Debt Transfer Agreement
data.description:
The latest update is out from Lvji Technology Holdings, Inc. ( (HK:1745) ).

Lvji Technology Holdings Inc. said shareholders passed all proposed resolutions at an extraordinary general meeting on November 19, 2026, by poll. They approved, confirmed and ratified a debt transfer agreement concerning the disposal of debts and authorised directors to execute related documents and take associated actions.

The agreement was between Lvji Technology Group Co., Ltd. as transferor and Guangzhou Ning’ao Xincheng Consulting Services Partnership (Limited Partnership) as transferee. The resolutions received 11,973,831 votes in favour, or 89.9803%, and 1,333,332 against, or 10.0197%.
